articles.title: Understanding Binary Search Trees
articles.content:
A binary search tree (BST) stores ordered data so lookups, inserts, and deletes average O(log n).

Each node has at most two children. Left subtree values are smaller; right subtree values are larger.

## Why balance matters
If you insert sorted data into a naive BST, the tree becomes a linked list and operations degrade to O(n).

Self-balancing trees such as AVL trees and red-black trees restructure after updates to keep height logarithmic.

## Takeaway
BSTs shine when order and structure matter. Prefer a balanced variant when input may arrive sorted.

articles.title: React Hooks without the magic
articles.content:
Hooks let function components hold state and side effects without converting them to classes.

## useState
Returns a value and a setter. Calling the setter schedules a re-render with the next state value.

## useEffect
Runs after paint for synchronization with the outside world such as subscriptions and network calls.

## Rules
Only call hooks at the top level of React functions. Do not call hooks inside loops or conditions.

Custom hooks can reuse stateful logic across components while following the same rules.

articles.title: RAG in plain English
articles.content:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounds an LLM in your documents instead of relying only on parametric memory.

## Pipeline
1. Chunk documents into passages
2. Embed chunks into vectors
3. Retrieve similar chunks for a question
4. Generate an answer with citations to those chunks

Weak retrieval should lead to refusal rather than unsupported claims.

On Quilio, Chat with a blog uses this idea for per-article grounded answers.

articles.title: JWT Authentication Basics
articles.content:
JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are compact tokens used for authentication between clients and APIs.

A JWT has three parts: header, payload, and signature, separated by dots.

Servers sign tokens with a secret. Clients send the token in the Authorization Bearer header.

Tokens should expire. Never store API secrets in the frontend. Validate signature and claims on every protected request.

Refresh tokens can extend sessions more carefully than long-lived access tokens. Rotate secrets if compromise is suspected.

articles.title: Embedding Pipelines for Learning Apps
articles.content:
An embedding pipeline turns article text into vectors for retrieval-augmented features.

Typical steps: normalize text, split into chunks, call an embedding model, store vectors with model and dimension metadata.

Query embeddings must use the same model and dimension as document vectors or similarity scores are meaningless.

A minimum similarity threshold can reject weak matches so the system refuses questions the article does not support.

Re-index after changing embedding models because vector spaces are incompatible across models.
